main_text.p: coqui. Infibro, priori parte pro carne, posteriori vero pro pifce vefcuntur nationes quaedam: de viteriori in re alimentaria potentia nihil aut patum conftat. Caeterum Caftorii, h.e. Caftoris feu fibri teftium exectorum, millenii in medicina vfus, Vide Plin. l. 32. c. 3. Diofcor. l. 2. c. 22.
Adhuc de alimentis quae veniunt ab nimalibus sanguineis, sequuntur sanguinis expertia.
main_text.head: CAP. XVIII.
main_text.p: Hic modi sunt sepiae, loligo, polypus item cruftacea, hoc est, cruftis cotecta, graecè μαλακόστρακα, vt cancer, squilla, locusta: Sc. necnon teftacea teftis inclusa, graeci ὀστρακόδερμα, vt limaces terrestres, cochleae, marinae, oftreae, pectines conchae.
main_text.head: De Sepia, Loligine, & Polypo.
main_text.p: Sepias, Polypos & Loligines germanice vocant Tintenfisch / Angli Cuttel/Kuttelfisch: catamen recte distinguuntur ftinguuntur longo major fit, ein grosser langer Blackfisch differentiam loliginis minoris, lepia generatim Blackfisch nominatur: Polypus vero fit ein Blackfisch mit einem kleinem Leibe und langen Füssen, darauff gehen kan, quib. etiam à pri ribus discernitur, qui pedes habent breuiores, am-pliusq[?]
Lines of the German passage are partly illegible in the scan; the rendering of the black letter words is approximate.

page.notes: The page is a fairly clean scan. The German black letter passage, the last line of the sepia paragraph and the Greek are the least certain readings. The signature at the lower left is not legible enough to copy and is left out. Show-through from the reverse side appears faintly and is not transcribed.
